headline: High-risk shared-write and shell-capable pair: nullclaw can alter shared state while pathway is read-only, creating prompt-injection and cascading-error exposure if outputs are bridged.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: nullclaw can read/write filesystem, use MCP, and run browsers, so if its outputs are bridged into pathway via shared files or pipelines, injected instructions can propagate. pathway has no direct input surfaces, so the risk is interaction-dependent rather than default. The pair lacks documented provenance controls.
conditions: IF nullclaw writes attacker-controlled text into ~/.nullclaw/workspace/ and pathway ingests that file as instructions, injection is possible.
IF an external orchestrator copies nullclaw output into pathway input without provenance tags, prompt injection can propagate.
mitigations: Disable file-based handoff between the agents.
Add provenance labels to every bridged message.
Restrict nullclaw to trusted templates only.
Review any shared workspace files before pathway consumes them.

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw touches secrets, workspace files, and audit logs, but pathway has no filesystem read, network egress, or clipboard surfaces in the profile. That makes direct leakage from pathway unlikely; the main exposure is accidental placement of sensitive files into a shared workspace that pathway cannot itself exfiltrate. The pairwise blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF sensitive files are copied into a shared directory that pathway can access through an external wrapper, leakage risk increases.
IF pathway is wrapped by another service that forwards its inputs to a third party, the profile no longer bounds leakage.
mitigations: Keep secrets out of any shared workspace.
Mount separate directories for each agent.
Rotate any credentials that were already placed in nullclaw workspace files.
Audit logs for accidental secret inclusion.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: nullclaw has broad write, shell, git, and network capabilities, while pathway is read-only and network-disabled. There is little direct write-write conflict between the two profiles, but if an orchestrator gives pathway mutable access outside its profile, contention could arise. Uncertainty is low because pathway’s profile is explicitly restrictive.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants pathway write access to the same directory as nullclaw, file contention becomes possible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same git repository with write permissions, commit conflicts can occur.
mitigations: Keep pathway read-only.
Use separate working directories.
Avoid shared git checkouts.
Serialize any writes through one agent only.

D_cascading_error.rationale: nullclaw can generate and act on web or workspace content, and pathway may consume processed documents downstream. If pathway treats nullclaw output as authoritative, errors can cascade into multiple work products. The pair lacks built-in verification or locking in the profiles, so the interaction is plausible in default orchestration.
conditions: IF pathway ingests nullclaw-produced text without a verification step, downstream errors can cascade.
IF nullclaw-generated facts are used as source material for document processing, incorrect outputs can be amplified.
mitigations: Require human review before pathway consumes nullclaw output.
Add checksum or schema validation between agents.
Separate fact generation from document processing.
Log source provenance for every downstream artifact.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, with no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. The only compliance concern visible is nullclaw’s handling of secrets and logs; pathway’s profile does not show regulated-data handling. Because no cross-jurisdiction or certification conflict is evidenced, severity stays low.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is routed through nullclaw into a noncompliant deployment, compliance risk increases.
IF either agent is configured with a retention policy that exceeds the operator's policy, a mismatch exists.
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through the pair.
Document retention settings for both agents.
Confirm residency requirements before deployment.
Purge any sensitive logs after testing.
